rows.opportunity: Retention and outcome measurement for essential services
rows.source_class: official company pages; company-reported scale and customer claims
rows.observed_facts: Trella describes an AI-enabled intelligence and workflow platform for health systems and post-acute providers. Its hospital solution connects discharge automation, provider visibility, referral workflows, and performance reporting.
rows.measurable_outcome_claim: Trella states that its workflows target discharge delays, readmissions, placement accuracy, capacity, and financial performance; the public pages also report scale and customer coverage.
rows.evidence_limits: Most scale, customer, and outcome statements are company-reported; public evidence does not establish customer retention, margin, causal outcome lift, or willingness to pay.
rows.assessment: supports pain and workflow wedge; outcome and durability proof pending
rows.durability_status: not established; test specified in opportunity protocol

rows.opportunity: Sell-through and margin visibility for growing brands

buyer_proxy_rows.opportunity: Retention and outcome measurement for essential services
buyer_proxy_rows.research_mode: public case-study proxy, not interview
buyer_proxy_rows.buyer_signal: A health plan used an end-to-end transportation platform to manage member rides and improve member experience, indicating a budget-bearing payer/operator use case.
buyer_proxy_rows.pain_signal: The case-study framing centers on cancellations, grievances, fulfillment, fraud/waste/abuse, and visibility across the ride journey.
buyer_proxy_rows.outcome_signal: SafeRide reports reductions in cancellation/grievance measures and high fulfillment; its Lyft case study reports 63% fewer no-shows and 30% lower call-center volume.
buyer_proxy_rows.procurement_signal: The product is offered as self-managed, fully managed, or hybrid infrastructure with integrations and compliance controls, indicating enterprise implementation and procurement friction.
buyer_proxy_rows.limitation: The case study is vendor-produced; sample, baseline, causal design, price, renewal terms, and independent verification are unknown.

buyer_proxy_rows.opportunity: Sell-through and margin visibility for growing brands
buyer_proxy_rows.research_mode: public vendor case study with named operator, not interview
buyer_proxy_rows.buyer_signal: A supplement brand used distributed fulfillment and EDI integrations for DTC and retail partners, showing a buyer with cross-channel inventory, fulfillment, and cost visibility needs.
buyer_proxy_rows.pain_signal: The operator needed to scale order volume, automate B2B retailer fulfillment, reduce transit time and fulfillment cost, and maintain order accuracy as channels expanded.

buyer_proxy_rows.procurement_signal: The purchase combines inventory placement, fulfillment operations, EDI, and multi-channel data, indicating a budget-bearing infrastructure decision rather than a dashboard-only purchase.
buyer_proxy_rows.limitation: The case does not provide SKU-level sell-through, retailer deductions, contribution margin, repeat purchase, CAC, or an independent comparison against alternatives.

buyer_proxy_rows.research_mode: public customer spotlight, not interview
buyer_proxy_rows.buyer_signal: A multi-technician home-service operator chose a pay-per-lead marketplace because it delivered real-time calls directly to the business and helped keep technicians productive.
buyer_proxy_rows.pain_signal: The operator described difficulty converting purchased customer information into booked work and the need to avoid chasing unqualified leads.
buyer_proxy_rows.outcome_signal: The vendor reports that 68% of appointments became jobs for this customer; the result is company-reported and does not isolate scheduling software from lead quality.
buyer_proxy_rows.procurement_signal: The buyer selected a flexible pay-per-lead service and could adjust lead volume, indicating a measurable operating purchase tied to capacity utilization.
buyer_proxy_rows.limitation: This is vendor-produced customer evidence about lead generation, not a direct test of technician scheduling, overtime, travel, safety, or completion economics.
